int_name: FOUR FREEDOMS HOME & W WALNUT LN

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a wide, paved sidewalk on a bridge with integrated artwork, protected by a low decorative wall and railing. The intersection ahead is controlled by traffic signals and includes a marked crosswalk, though the immediate roadway surface is obscured by digital blurring.

hazards.name: Low Bridge Railing
hazards.description: The decorative railing on the bridge appears relatively low, potentially posing a fall risk for some users.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side, along the edge of the sidewalk.

hazards.name: Visual Clutter from Overhead Wires
hazards.description: Extensive overhead utility wires create visual noise and potential distractions for both drivers and pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Upper half of the image across the sky.

interventions.title: Heightened Safety Railing
interventions.description: Install a taller, more robust safety fence or railing along the bridge edge to prevent accidental falls.

interventions.title: Undergrounding Utilities
interventions.description: Relocate overhead power and communication lines underground to improve aesthetics and reduce visual distractions.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a high-visibility marked crosswalk and a well-maintained sidewalk with a decorative mural. However, the crossing is uncontrolled and lacks a refuge island, which increases exposure for pedestrians on this wide roadway.

hazards.name: Uncontrolled Crossing
hazards.description: The lack of active signals or stop signs requires pedestrians to judge gaps in traffic on a wide road.

hazards.name: Wide Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The distance across the roadway is significant without a mid-point refuge, increasing exposure time to vehicles.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Reduces crossing distance and provides a safe haven for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Shortens the crossing distance and increases pedestrian visibility to drivers.

interventions.title: Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons (RRFB)
interventions.description: Increases driver yielding rates at uncontrolled crossings.

result.summary: The image shows a signalized intersection with a high-visibility zebra crosswalk and a sidewalk. The road curves significantly at the crossing point, and the surrounding area is heavily wooded, which may impact sightlines for approaching vehicles.

hazards.name: Curved Roadway Sightlines
hazards.description: The sharp curve in the road may limit the ability of drivers to see pedestrians in the crosswalk until they are close.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image where the road curves away into the trees.

hazards.name: Pavement Degradation
hazards.description: Cracking in the asphalt within the crosswalk area could present a minor tripping hazard.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground, within the white stripes of the crosswalk.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised median or refuge island to reduce the unprotected crossing distance and provide a safe waiting area mid-crossing.

interventions.title: Advance Warning Signage
interventions.description: Install 'Pedestrian Crossing' warning signs with flashing beacons ahead of the curve to alert drivers to the upcoming crossing.

interventions.title: Pavement Repair
interventions.description: Resurface the intersection to eliminate cracks and provide a smooth, level walking surface for pedestrians.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a marked crosswalk and a sidewalk in good condition adjacent to a large residential building. However, sight lines at the crossing are partially obstructed by a fence and a large tree, and there is a lack of active pedestrian signaling or high-visibility markings.

hazards.name: Sight line obstruction
hazards.description: A large tree and a black chain-link fence at the corner may block the view between drivers and pedestrians waiting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image at the corner near the apartment building

hazards.name: Low-visibility crosswalk
hazards.description: The existing transverse crosswalk markings are faded and less visible to approaching drivers than high-visibility patterns.

interventions.title: High-visibility crosswalk markings
interventions.description: Replace the existing transverse lines with continental or ladder-style markings to increase visibility to approaching drivers.

interventions.title: Curb extension
interventions.description: Install a curb extension on the corner to move pedestrians further into the roadway before crossing, improving their visibility to drivers and shortening the crossing distance.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Ensure the area immediately preceding the crosswalk is kept clear of any additional obstructions to maintain the best possible sight lines.
